title: How a hot-air balloon rises and sinks
examples: How does a hot-air balloon float?
How do hot-air balloons come down?
Can you steer a hot-air balloon?

explain.say: A hot-air balloon floats because hot air is lighter than cold air. Heating the air inside the envelope makes it spread out, so the balloon holds less mass than the same space of cool air outside.

draw.text: How a hot-air balloon rises and sinks

explain.say: The cooler, heavier air outside pushes the balloon upwards with a force called buoyancy. When buoyancy is bigger than the weight of the balloon, basket and people, it rises.
To go down, the pilot stops burning or opens a vent at the top to let hot air out. The air inside cools, buoyancy becomes smaller than the weight, and the balloon sinks.
Balloons have no steering wheel: they drift with the wind. Pilots steer by climbing or sinking to find winds blowing in different directions at different heights.

faq.a: Heating air makes its molecules move faster and spread out, so a space full of hot air weighs less than the same space of cold air. The heavier cold air around it sinks and pushes the hot air up.
asks: How does a hot-air balloon float?

faq.q: How does a hot-air balloon go down?
faq.a: The pilot lets the air cool or pulls a cord that opens a vent at the top to let hot air out. With less hot air, buoyancy drops below the weight and the balloon descends.

faq.q: How do you steer a hot-air balloon?
faq.a: You can't steer it directly; it moves with the wind. Pilots change height to catch winds blowing in different directions, which lets them choose their path a little.
asks: Can a hot-air balloon be steered?

faq.q: What fuel does a balloon burner use?
faq.a: Most use propane gas from tanks in the basket. The burner roars in bursts, keeping the air inside the envelope at around 100 degrees Celsius.
asks: How hot is the air in a hot-air balloon?

faq.q: Why do balloons fly in the early morning?
faq.a: Winds are usually calm in the early morning and evening, and there are fewer bumpy rising air currents. That makes take-off and landing safer.

facts: The first people to fly were carried by a Montgolfier hot-air balloon over Paris in 1783.
Air heated to about 100 degrees Celsius is around a fifth lighter than the same volume of air at 20 degrees.

quiz.show: Firing the burner makes the balloon…
quiz.why: Heating makes the air inside lighter, so buoyancy beats weight and the balloon climbs.

wrong.1: Sinking happens when the air inside cools, not when it is heated.
wrong.2: The burner changes height, not direction.
